description: The contract for the ward and district profile exports: every column, its unit, source, data year, uncertainty class and what a blank means.

official_count.label: Official count
official_count.meaning: A count published by an official body for a stated geography and year. It counts registered cases or reported crashes, not everything that happened.

mapped_osm.label: Mapped in OpenStreetMap
mapped_osm.meaning: A count of features volunteers have mapped in OpenStreetMap. It is a lower bound: a zero or a low count can mean the area is not mapped, not that the facility is absent.

approximate_position.label: Depends on approximate positions
approximate_position.meaning: Depends on crash-zone positions placed by hand at landmark centres; the Traffic Police publish no coordinates. Each zone carries its own estimated accuracy (150 m to 5 km), so a zone can fall in the wrong ward.

survey.label: Survey, partial coverage
survey.meaning: From a survey that did not cover every district. A blank means not surveyed, not zero.

derived.label: Derived here
derived.meaning: Computed in this project from other fields by the rule stated in the field description. It inherits the uncertainty of its inputs.

district_inherited.label: District value copied to wards
district_inherited.meaning: Crime is published only per police district, so every ward in a district shows the same figure. It says nothing about differences between wards.

geometry.label: Boundary, not official
geometry.meaning: From the legacy 290-ward boundary file (DataMeet, before the 2022 delimitation). It is not an official or current boundary.

identifier.label: Identifier
identifier.meaning: A name or number used to identify the row.

general: Why crashes happened, or that any facility here caused or would prevent them.
Risk per person or per trip: there are no pedestrian or traffic counts, so counts are not rates of risk.
That a place without mapped infrastructure has none: OpenStreetMap coverage is uneven.
Crime by ward: crime is published only for the 15 police districts.
Anything about the current 250 MCD wards: these profiles use the legacy 290-ward geography.
A change over time for a ward or a named zone: boundaries, zone lists and mapping all change between years.
Who is responsible for a location, or what should be built there. Field verification is needed before any intervention.

byClass.approximate_position: Where exactly crashes happened, or that a crash-prone zone lies inside this ward rather than next to it.
byClass.mapped_osm: How much of the facility actually exists on the ground.
byClass.district_inherited: Whether this ward is better or worse than its neighbours in the same district.
byClass.survey: Anything about districts the survey did not cover.
byClass.official_count: The true level of crime or crashes: counts depend on reporting and registration.
